body_markdown:
Chevrolet has a great record of building tremendous performance into the Corvette while keeping it affordable enough to be both aspirational and attainable for enthusiasts. When the eighth-generation Corvette debuted in 2019, Chevrolet shocked everyone by offering a 490-hp, mid-engine sports car with a starting price under $60,000. Unfortunately, what the C8 Corvette didn’t offer was a manual transmission.


Starting now, C8 owners can line up for a six-speed manual conversion thanks to Tremec and Peitz Performance. Alex Peitz founded[Peitz Performance](https://www.peitzperformancetunes.com/) in Houston, Texas, with the goal of supplying C8 parts for those pushing the envelope of power and speed. He’s worked to develop dry-sump oiling systems, exhausts, coil-over suspensions, conversions for fitting 15-inch wheels for drag tires, and plug-and-play ECUs, just to name a few. The manual C8 Corvette conversion was a big undertaking, but Alex knows his way around a C8 by now.


[Brandan Gillogly](https://www.hagerty.com/media/author/brandan-gillogly/)


We[discussed the new six-speed transaxle last year](https://www.hagerty.com/media/news/tremec-unveils-a-6-speed-manual-transaxle-c8-owners-rejoice/) after Tremec showed off its prototype at the 2025 Specialty Equipment Aftermarket Association (SEMA) show. Tremec told us that while the prototypes feature billet aluminum housings, the company is tooling up to produce the housings in cast aluminum. Tremec developed the transaxle with the aftermarket in mind. Kit-car manufacturers like Factory Five were looking to offer solutions for customers building high-performance, high-horsepower cars. There just weren’t many solutions for those looking for a transaxle that could hold up to a modern, supercharged V-8. This new TR-9060 can withstand 1000 lb-ft of torque and engine speeds up to 8600 rpm.


Tremec was able to streamline the development of this new TR-9060 by adapting the differential from the C8’s dual-clutch transaxle. This new piece also borrows heavily from the gears and synchros used in the TR-6060. As with any high-performance part made in relatively small batches, the TR-9060 will not come cheap. Tremec expects pricing to be somewhere around $20,000. That’s not counting all of the new electronics required to keep everything in the car working as expected in a late-model car like a C8 Corvette. There’s also an intensive installation process.[Peitz Performance is quoting just under $75,000 for the conversion](https://www.peitzperformancetunes.com/products/c8-manual-transmission-swap) . Those building 1000-hp race cars should expect to pay up for parts that can withstand that kind of punishment.


[Brandan Gillogly](https://www.hagerty.com/media/author/brandan-gillogly/)


We spoke with Alex Peitz at the Tremec booth at the 2026 SEMA show. He walked us through some of the challenges of the swap, from fitting a clutch master cylinder in a firewall never designed for one to getting the shifter just right. “The shifter started off life as a Porsche aftermarket shifter,” Alex said, pointing out the welded-aluminum jungle gym that holds the lever and cable. “There’s about 20% of that shifter left now.” Even though it required a lot of modification, the Porsche shifter served as a good jumping-off point and saved a lot of fabrication time. It will fit in the C8 after relocating the drive mode dial.


He used a similar approach for the clutch pedal. “That started off as a[CT4-V Blackwing](https://www.hagerty.com/media/new-car-reviews/review-the-cadillac-ct4-v-blackwing-dials-in-everything-about-the-ats-v/) pedal,” he explained, “but there’s not much of that left, either. We’re gonna go back and make a production-friendly piece.” Using the Cadillac clutch enables Peitz to link it to a Motec M150. The ECU handles the transaxle’s electronics and communicates with the engine over a CAN bus. That allows the engine to cut ignition spark for no-lift upshifts and blip the throttle for downshifts.


Tremec expects to have a batch of TR-9060 transaxles in production by next summer. Peitz Performance has already heard from some potential customers interested in the conversion. Peitz’s Corvette will definitely have some three-pedal compatriots by the time the 2027 SEMA rolls around.


[Brandan Gillogly](https://www.hagerty.com/media/author/brandan-gillogly/)
